detail.longDescription: I work on python with polars. I have: A dataframe df with columns mc1 and mc2 and A dictionary dico . I would like to filter on df to keep only the rows for which mc1 is an existing key of dico and dico[mc1] == mc2 . Is it possible? I firstly tried something like this: import polars as pl import numpy as np df = pl.DataFrame({'mc1':[1,2,3,4], 'mc2':[5,6,7,8]}) dico = {1:5,2:2,4:8} df.filter(pl.col('mc1').is_in(dico.keys()) & (dico[pl.col('mc1')] == pl.col('mc2'))) But it didn't work. I also tried to produce a list of booleans indicating which row to keep, like it would work using pandas, doing this: mask = np.zeros(len(df),dtype=bool) for i in range(len(df)): mc = df['mc1'][i] mask[i] = (mc in dico) and (df['mc2'][i] == dico[mc]) And it succeeded, but then I don't know how to use this mask : looks like the pandas syntax df[mask] doesn't work. Do you have a solution?
